heading: Liji 21 · Ji Yi 祭義 · The Meaning Of Sacrifices · Ji Yi II.7 … Ji Yi II.10

items.text: Offer the silkworm-made robes in sacrifice to the former kings and dukes with the utmost reverence.
items.quote: the ruler wore them in sacrificing to the former kings and dukes;--all displayed the greatest reverence.
items.conflict: Sacrifice belongs to God alone; offerings to the dead are forbidden.

items.text: Oversee the silkworm work so that finished robes are ready for your husband's sacrifices.
items.quote: Will not these supply the materials for the ruler's robes?

items.text: Honor your parents as the highest degree of filial piety.
items.quote: The highest is the honouring of our parents

items.text: Do nothing that would bring disgrace upon your parents.
items.quote: the second is the not disgracing them

items.text: Support your parents in their needs; this is the lowest degree of filial piety.
items.quote: the lowest is the being able to support them

items.text: Anticipate your parents' wishes, carry out their aims, and follow their instruction in the path of duty.
items.quote: requires the anticipation of our parents' wishes, the carrying out of their aims and their instruction in the path

heading: Liji 21 · Ji Yi 祭義 · The Meaning Of Sacrifices · Ji Yi I.19 … Ji Yi II.6

items.text: Remember your ancestors and go back to your oldest fathers; do not forget those to whom you owe your being.
items.quote: teaching the people to go back to their oldest fathers, and retrace their beginnings, not forgetting those to whom they owed their being.
items.conflict: Worship of ancestors is forbidden; honor parents while living (Exod 20:12; Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Call forth all reverence and exhaust your strength in discharging the service to your departed parents as a tribute of gratitude.
items.quote: he calls forth all his reverence, gives free vent to his feelings, and exhausts his strength in discharging the above service;--as a tribute of gratitude to his parents he dares not but do his utmost.
items.conflict: Sacrifices to the dead are idolatrous (1 Cor 10:20); gratitude is expressed by honoring living parents.

items.text: Personally labor to provide offerings for your ancestors, as an expression of great reverence.
items.quote: the son of Heaven had his field of a thousand acres, in which he himself held the plough... in the service of... their ancient fathers
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are not required; Christ is the only mediator (1 Tim 2:5).

items.text: Keep sacrificial animals and personally inspect them, choosing only spotless and perfect victims.
items.quote: they washed their heads, bathed, and visited them in person, taking from them for victims those which were spotless and perfect
items.conflict: Animal sacrifices ended in Christ (Heb 10:1-14); no sacrifice to the dead.

items.text: Divine whether the sacrificial animals are acceptable, and inspect them monthly with utmost care.
items.quote: he chose them by their hair, divined whether it would be fortunate to use them... on the first day and at the middle of the month, he inspected them.
items.conflict: Divination is forbidden (Deut 18:10-12); filial piety does not require superstition.

heading: Liji 21 · Ji Yi 祭義 · The Meaning Of Sacrifices · Ji Yi II.11 … Ji Yi II.17

items.text: Conduct yourself gravely at home, loyally in service, reverently in office, sincerely with friends, and bravely in battle, so that no disgrace reaches your parents.
items.quote: if in his own house and privacy be not grave, he is not filial... if he fail in these five things, the evil (of the disgrace) will reach his parents

items.text: Support your parents not merely with food but with reverence, without self-constraint, and maintain it to the end.
items.quote: To prepare the fragrant flesh and grain... is not filial piety; it is only nourishing them... support them; the difficulty is in doing so with the proper reverence.

items.text: After your parents' death, watch over your actions so that no bad name involving them is handed down.
items.quote: When his parents are dead, and the son carefully watches over his actions, so that a bad name, (involving) his parents, shall not be handed down

items.text: Serve your parents with your strength, endure toil for them, and never fail in this service.
items.quote: three degrees of filial piety:--the least, seen in the employment of one's strength... the second, seen in the endurance of toil... the greatest, seen in its never failing.

items.text: When your parents love you, rejoice and never forget them; when they hate you, fear but hold no resentment; when they have faults, remonstrate but do not withstand them.
items.quote: When his parents love him, to rejoice... when they hate him, to fear and yet feel no resentment; when they have faults, to remonstrate with them, and yet not withstand them

items.text: When obtaining grain for the ancestral sacrifice, ask help only from the good.
items.quote: when they are dead, to ask (the help only of) the good to obtain the grain with which to sacrifice to them
items.conflict: Sacrificing to the dead conflicts with the biblical command to worship God alone (Deut 26:14; Ps 106:28).

items.text: Preserve your body whole and undefiled, for your parents gave it to you complete; return it to them complete.
items.quote: His parents give birth to his person all complete, and to return it to them all complete may be called filial duty. When no member has been mutilated and no disgrace done to any part of the person, it may be called complete.

items.text: Never forget your parents in any step or word; avoid perilous paths and choose safe ways, and keep evil or angry words from your mouth so as not to shame them.
items.quote: should not forget his parents in a single lifting up of his feet... therefore he will walk in the highway... an evil word will not issue from his mouth... Not to disgrace his person and not to cause shame to his parents may be called filial duty.

items.text: Submit to your older brother, yield precedence, and follow behind him.
items.quote: Thus the submission of a younger brother (and juniors generally) was recognised at the court.

items.text: Honor the aged as next to serving your parents; yield to them and do not burden them.
items.quote: For long has honour been paid to years under the sky; to pay it is next to the service of parents.

items.text: Do not fell trees or kill animals except at the proper seasons, for doing so is contrary to filial piety.
items.quote: To fell a single tree, or kill a single animal, not at the proper season, is contrary to filial piety.

heading: Liji 21 · Ji Yi 祭義 · The Meaning Of Sacrifices · Ji Yi I.1 … Ji Yi I.8

items.text: Offer the sacrifices of spring and autumn with measured frequency, neither too often nor too seldom, so that reverence is maintained.
items.quote: Sacrifices should not be frequently repeated... offers the sacrifices of spring and autumn.
items.conflict: Ancestral sacrifices violate the first commandment; worship is due to God alone.

items.text: During the vigil before sacrifice, recall their manner of life, their words, and their desires until you seem to see them.
items.quote: During the days of such vigil, the mourner thinks of his departed, how and where they sat, how they smiled and spoke, what were their aims and views.
items.conflict: Seeking visions of the dead through imaginative recollection is a form of necromancy (Deut. 18:10-12).

items.text: Keep in memory your parents' looks, voices, aims, likings, and wishes; do not let them fade.
items.quote: the eyes of the son should not forget the looks, nor his ears their voices; and that he should retain the memory of their aims, likings, and wishes.

items.text: While your parents are alive, reverently nourish them.
items.quote: while (his parents) are alive, reverently nourishes them.

items.text: When your parents are dead, reverently sacrifice to them, as you nourished them in life.
items.quote: when they are dead, he reverently sacrifices to them.
items.conflict: Sacrifice to the dead is idolatry; only God is to be worshiped.

items.text: To the end of life, do nothing to disgrace your parents.
items.quote: his (chief) thought is how to the end of life not to disgrace them.

items.text: On the anniversary of their death, set aside your ordinary work and keep your thoughts occupied with them.
items.quote: That he does not do his ordinary work on that day... his thoughts are occupied with them.
items.conflict: Ancestor commemoration can become a rival religious practice, displacing faith in Christ.

items.text: In the ancestral sacrifice, lead the offering of the victim and present the offerings to the personator.
items.quote: the ruler leads the victim forward... presents the offerings to the personator.
items.conflict: Offering sacrifices to ancestors is forbidden; the living have no communion with the dead.

items.text: Assist your husband in the sacrifice by arranging the bowls and dishes.
items.quote: his wife puts down the bowls... sets forth the various dishes.
items.conflict: Participating in idolatrous ancestral rites is contrary to God's law.

items.text: In sacrificing to your own parents, seek inner communion with their spirits, not outward formality.
items.quote: How should such demeanour consist with communion with the spirits (sacrificed to)?
items.conflict: Seeking communion with spirits of the dead is necromancy (Deut. 18:11).

heading: Liji 21 · Ji Yi 祭義 · The Meaning Of Sacrifices · Ji Yi I.9 … Ji Yi I.18

items.text: Perform the ancestral sacrifice with all preparations complete, with utmost reverence, sincerity, and gravity at every stage, seeking communion with the dead.
items.citation: Liji, Ji Yi I.9 … Ji Yi I.18
items.quote: he is anxious that all preparations should be made beforehand; and when the time arrives, that everything necessary should be found complete
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is idolatry; only God may be worshiped (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Husband and wife, after vigil and bathing, in full dress, carry in the offerings with the utmost gravity and absorption.
items.citation: Liji, Ji Yi I.9 … Ji Yi I.18
items.quote: husband and wife, after vigil and footing, bathe their heads and persons, and array themselves in full dress... how grave and still are they!
items.conflict: Ancestor worship is idolatry; only God may be worshiped (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Serve your parents with deep love, mild and compliant demeanor, and grave carefulness; not with austere severity.
items.citation: Liji, Ji Yi I.9 … Ji Yi I.18
items.quote: cherishing a deep love (for his parents), is sure to have a bland air... A severe gravity and austere manner are not proper to the service of parents

items.text: Honor the old and revere the aged, for they approximate the positions of parents and elder brothers.
items.citation: Liji, Ji Yi I.9 … Ji Yi I.18
items.quote: honour which they paid to the virtuous; to the noble; and to the old; the reverence which they showed to the aged

items.text: Be kind to the young, for they approximate the position of sons.
items.citation: Liji, Ji Yi I.9 … Ji Yi I.18
items.quote: kindness to the young, because of their approximation to the position of sons

items.text: Revere your father, as even the Son of Heaven reveres his father.
items.citation: Liji, Ji Yi I.9 … Ji Yi I.18
items.quote: even the son of Heaven had the father (whom he must revere)

items.text: Obey your elder brother, as even a feudal lord obeys his elder brothers.
items.citation: Liji, Ji Yi I.9 … Ji Yi I.18
items.quote: even a feudal lord had his elder brothers (or cousins), (whom he must obey)

items.text: Love your parents as the foundation of all love and value them properly.
items.citation: Liji, Ji Yi I.9 … Ji Yi I.18
items.quote: The laying the foundation of (all) love in the love of parents teaches people concord... the people set the (proper) value on their parents

items.text: Revere your elders and obey the orders given to you.
items.citation: Liji, Ji Yi I.9 … Ji Yi I.18
items.quote: reverence of elders teaches the people obedience... obeying the orders given to them

items.text: Assist your father in the sacrificial rites, as the ruler's son assists him.
items.citation: Liji, Ji Yi I.9 … Ji Yi I.18
items.quote: the ruler led the victim forward, along with and assisted by his son on the opposite side

heading: Liji 21 · Ji Yi 祭義 · The Meaning Of Sacrifices · Ji Yi II.18 … Ji Yi II.27

items.text: Yield to your elders in hunts and army by giving them a larger share and better place according to age.
items.quote: a larger share was given to the more aged

items.text: Practice filial duty in the court, on the road, in districts and hamlets, in hunts, and in the army.
items.quote: The display of filial and fraternal duty in the court

items.text: Practice fraternal submission to your elder sibling in all settings, from court to army.
items.quote: The display of filial and fraternal duty in the court

items.text: At meetings of all the members of a clan, give precedence to anyone who is seventy years old, regardless of rank.
items.quote: at meetings of all the members of a clan no one dared to take precedence of one who was seventy years old

items.text: Pay regard to age in country and villages; do not neglect the old and poor.
items.quote: regard was paid to age, that the old and poor were not neglected

items.text: Ascribe the ground of whatever good you possess to your parents, and its preservation to your elders.
items.quote: he assigned the ground of it to his parents, and the preservation of it to his elders

items.text: Prepare for the ancestral sacrifice with a grave and adjusted mind, providing robes and repairing the temple.
items.quote: his mind well adjusted and grave, to fit him for giving to all matters their full consideration, for providing the robes and other things, for repairing the temple
items.conflict: Ancestral rites conflict with the First Commandment and Deut. 18:10-12.

items.text: On the day of sacrifice, be mild in countenance and show anxious dread, as if you fear your love is not sufficient.
items.quote: his countenance should be mild, and his movements show an anxious dread, as if he feared his love were not sufficient
items.conflict: Ancestral rites conflict with the First Commandment and Deut. 18:10-12.

items.text: When offering, bend your body as if your parents would speak, and stand reverently as if about to lose sight of them.
items.quote: his demeanour should be mild, and his body bent, as if (his parents) would speak (to him) and had not yet done so
items.conflict: Ancestral rites conflict with the First Commandment and Deut. 18:10-12.

items.text: After the sacrifice, look pleased and expectant, as if your deceased parents would again enter.
items.quote: After the sacrifice, he looked pleased and expectant, as if they would again enter.
items.conflict: Ancestral rites conflict with the First Commandment and Deut. 18:10-12.

items.text: Let your thoughts never leave your parents; continually examine yourself in the way of a filial son.
items.quote: the exercises of his thoughts never left his parents... he was continually examining himself
items.conflict: Ancestral rites conflict with the First Commandment and Deut. 18:10-12.

items.text: When entering a school, even as the eldest son, take your place according to age, not rank.
items.quote: when his eldest son entered one of them, he took his place according to his age
